summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of liver transplant presented with acute worsening of dizziness and a new-onset headache, which began shortly after sitting up one morning. She described vertigo, unsteadiness, nausea, photophobia, and auditory hallucinations of whispering. Initial concern included stroke, but CT and MRI of the brain showed no hemorrhage, infarct, or vascular abnormality. Her symptoms were attributed to a likely adverse effect of atovaquone, which she had started three weeks prior. Her tacrolimus level was initially elevated but normalized during admission. Atovaquone was discontinued and replaced with dapsone, with plans to monitor white blood cell count. She improved with supportive care, including ondansetron for nausea and planned vestibular therapy. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in neurology and hepatology.
